hero.tagline: Know before your satellite goes dark.
hero.value: ArcWatch is a clip-on sensor that listens for small electrical arcs on satellite solar-array cables, without touching the conductor.
hero.alt: The ArcWatch clamp closed around a white solar-array cable

problem.label: The Problem
problem.title: Failure starts as a spark nobody sees.
problem.intro: An arc is a tiny electrical spark: current jumping across a small gap on the solar array. It can be over in an instant, or it can keep burning.[[masui]]

flow.title: Tested on the ground
flow.text: Arrays are tested on the ground to survive arcs before launch.[[ecss]]

flow.title: Small arcs in orbit
flow.text: Once in orbit, solar arrays can arc.[[elhameed]]

flow.title: Arcs grow
flow.text: Those arcs can grow into sustained arcs.[[elhameed]]

problem.gap: After launch, we found no operational monitor that watches for them.
problem.impact: The array is the satellite's power supply. Internet, weather and GPS services depend on those satellites.

product.label: The Product
product.title: It clips on. It listens. It never touches the conductor.
product.body: ArcWatch clips around a solar-array cable. A ring inside picks up the fast burst of noise an arc makes, and a small board counts each one and reports every string's trend to the satellite. Nothing is cut, and nothing touches the conductor.

tiers.name: Monitor
tiers.text: Counts arcs and shows each string's trend, so operators see trouble building.

tiers.name: Guard
tiers.text: Does everything Monitor does, and can ask the satellite's power controller for help. It never switches flight power itself.
